reader.requirement: At --std 85, in the ASSIGN clause of a sequential (and, by the identical VIII/IX rule, relative and indexed) file control entry, literal-1 must be a 1985 nonnumeric literal (1 to 160 characters, §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.1) and is refused when numeric (any sign or scale) or a figurative constant (ZERO, SPACE, QUOTE, HIGH-VALUE, LOW-VALUE, ALL literal); implementor-name-1 and the value of literal-1 are the implementor's; the witnesses cover "" and SPACE plus the device-class list, not numeric literals, the other figurative constants, relative/indexed entries or the 1985-only literal forms.

reader.notes: Every numeric and figurative-constant literal-1 is refused for sequential, relative and indexed entries at 85 via the deferred EntryShapeFindings that FileControlKeyRules.Screen reports for every non-SD entry. The zero-length literal draws two diagnostics (COBOL2645 and COBOL0900) for one fault, and every message cites §2023:12.4.5.2 SR4 rather than the 1985 rule; neither changes the verdict.

refuter.evidence: Probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-062/p3_assign_null-001 (--std 85): SELECT F1 ASSIGN TO NULL. -> error COBOL1639 "'NULL' is not defined ... §2023:8.9 does not reserve the word at this edition". At 85 NULL is not a reserved word (the 1985 reserved list has no NULL; the compiler's own message says so), so in this position it is implementor-name-1, a system-name, which needs no declaration (§1985:IV.4.2.2.1 SR1b: the same word may be a system-name and a user-defined word, classified by context). The implementation's own determination for implementor-name-1 (AssignTargetRule.WordText, DOC-A.1-71) admits any word as the file name, and it does so for every other word that a later edition reserves: p3_assign_nulls-001 (NULLS), p3_assign_typedef-001 (TYPEDEF), p3_assign_self-001 (SELF) compile and run, exit 0, DONE. The NULL token alone is parsed as nonNumericLiteral.predefinedNull at every edition and AssignTargetRule.Text sends it to PredefinedNullRule.Report, whose 85 arm (UnreservedKeywordReference) treats it as an undeclared data reference. At --std 2023 the same program draws COBOL2576 (correct there: NULL is the predefined identifier). Other probes upheld the reader: p3_assign_list-001 refuses ZERO/QUOTES/12 as a second list operand (COBOL2645) and N"..." (COBOL0900 + COBOL2645). cite.py: OK §1985:VII.2.3.3 SR3 the text is in SR3; OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.1 the text lies in SR1b. kb/Work: PB1673 (landed) fixed the 85 NULL diagnostic for VALUE and constant entries and made it 'not defined'; no note covers ASSIGN, where the word is a system-name, not a data reference.

refuter.corrected: NON-CONFORMING, rejects-legal-source, cause (a): at --std 85 ASSIGN TO NULL (NULL an unreserved COBOL word, so implementor-name-1) is refused with COBOL1639 while every other unreserved word is accepted as the file name; expected: accepted as implementor-name-1 like NULLS or TYPEDEF. At 2023 it is (correctly) COBOL2576. Known note: none (PB1673 is the nearest).

adjudication.reason: `ASSIGN TO NULL` is refused at 85 (COBOL1639 "not defined"); NULL is not a reserved word in 1985, so there it is an implementor-defined file name, as `ASSIGN TO NULLS` already is.
